Sean O'Toole

Systems Neuroscientist and Data Scientist, Basel, CH

Resume

About Me

A life sciences Ph.D. experienced with single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics, with a strong programming skillset, who can apply deep-learning techniques to NGS data as well as integrate external omics datasets to gain biological insights. A former experimentalist who transitioned to data science, I excel at experimental design and can capably collaborate with computational and bench scientists alike. A creative and dedicated worker, who is eager to solve difficult problems, and can rapidly adapt to new circumstances. I’m seeking to make an impact on the lives of medical patients through early-stage drug discovery.

Experience

Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics

Bioinformatician - July 2024 - Present

Utlized data science and Bioinformatics to work with patient datasets alongside the Translational Data Sceince group.

  • Building deep learning and classical machine learning models to predict the outcome of chemoradiotherapy treatment in rectal cancer patients based on NGS and microarray data sets.
  • Examining the cellular and gene expression composition of tumors derived from clinical samples using spatial transcriptomics, to generate testable hypotheses for breast cancer research.
  • Communicating with pathologists, specialists, and bioinformaticians to achieve research goals.
Deep Learning Machine Learning Bulk RNA sequencing analysis Spatial transcriptomics analysis Python R Git Statistics

Friedrich Miescher Institute

Postdoctoral Fellow - November 2017 - December 2023

Systems neuroscientist examining the relationship between computational models of neocortical function and transcriptionally defined cell types.

  • Generated and analyzed large-scale single-cell RNA sequencing data sets for the selection of biomarkers utilized in the development of cell-type specific AAVs.
  • Integrated in-house single-cell RNA sequencing with neural activity levels as well as public datasets to map transcriptionally defined cell types to computational roles.
  • Routinely presented findings to an interdisciplinary team as well as at high-profile meetings.
  • Designed computational workflows for preprocessing, cleaning, and manipulating large-scale data sets.
Single-cell RNA-sequecing R Python LabVIEW Matlab Calcium Imaging Histology

Education / Training

Brandeis University

Neuroscience Ph.D. - Degree completed 2017

As a doctoral student I examined the role of post-transcriptional (microRNAs) regulation in the development of epilepsy as the maintenance of cellular identity in spinal cord neurons. You can click here to download my thesis and read more about my findings.
  • Designed, analyzed and interpreted experiments in the context of preclinical disease models.
  • Initiated and managed an interdisciplinary collaboration to gain assistance with spinal cord electrophysiology experiments (outside the lab's area of expertise).
  • Mentored 2 master’s students and 2 undergraduate students, one of whom won an award for best thesis.

Worcester Polytechnic Institute

Molecular Biology and Biotechnology - Degree completed 2008

Earned a Bachelor of Science with distinction.
  • Conducted a yeat two-hyrbid screen, to examine protein to protein interactions to better understand the moelcular network dirving neuronal cell migration and process out growth in C. elegans which led to identification or an interaction pair and contributed to a scientific publication.
  • Developed and taught two course series aimed at introducing and preparing undergraduates for the reading of classic primary literature sources within the field of biology.
